question: A product is sold at a 20% discount on its marked price. This transaction results in a profit of 10% on its cost price. If the profit earned is ₹300, what would have been the selling price if the product was sold at a 30% discount on its marked price?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Profit = 10% of CP = ₹300 ⇒ CP = ₹3000

First Selling Price (SP₁) = CP + Profit = 3000 + 300 = ₹3300

Since SP₁ is after a 20% discount, SP₁ corresponds to 80% of Marked Price (MP).

New Selling Price after a 30% discount will correspond to 70% of MP.

New SP = SP₁ × (70 ÷ 80) = 3300 × (7 ÷ 8) = ₹2887.50

**∴ The correct answer is ₹2887.50.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Profit % = 10%

Discount % = 20%

Profit earned = ₹300

**Formula Used:**

Profit = (Profit% ÷ 100) × Cost Price (CP)

Selling Price (SP) = CP + Profit = Marked Price (MP) × (100 − Discount%) ÷ 100
